title: SLO partnerships runbook for product integrations and vendor dependencies
content:
Purpose:
This is a practical runbook for onboarding, monitoring, and operating partner/product integrations that have dependencies on Redwood’s inference surface (hosted API, Dedicated, Private). Focus: avoid SLO regressions caused by third-party SDKs, vendor infra changes, and product integration releases.

Scope:
- Applies to any external integration (3rd-party SDKs, partner connectors, managed data pipelines) that directly or indirectly affects request latency, error rate, or correctness (model mismatch/regression).
- Includes partner rollout plans, vendor upgrade windows, and product feature launches that touch routing, batching, or caching.
- Excludes internal-only infra changes that are covered by platform release playbooks (but see crosswalk below).

Background / motivation (notes to self):
- We saw two incidents in Q4 where downstream SDK retries + request batching changes amplified latency spikes and caused error budgets to burn.
- Partners often ship changes on different cadence; we need a light-weight pattern for alignment and gating.
- Goal: predictable activation cadence, small blast radius, and measurable signal plumbing before full traffic.

Goals & success criteria:
- No more than one major SLO breach attributable to partner/integration per quarter.
- 90% of new partner integrations pass the "integration readiness checklist" before production traffic.
- Dashboard coverage (latency P95, error-rate, model-quality drift) for every active integration within 48 hours of onboarding.

SLOs impacted (example catalog):
- Frontend request success rate (SLO: 99.95% 30d rolling) — common failure mode: partner retries overwhelm pool.
- Inference tail latency (SLO: P95 < 250ms for small requests) — common failure: vendor SDK batching + long-tail GC.
- Model quality regression (SLO: no >3% drop in pass-rate on monitoring prompts) — common failure: unexpected model variant fallback.

Roles & responsibilities (working allocation):
- Integration Owner (product manager or partner PM): coordinates partner-side testing, provides release windows, owns acceptance.
- SRE Partner Liaison (SRE): configures dashboards, sets alerts, runs canary automation, signs off on rollout gates.
- Runtime Engineer: verifies batching/kv-cache behaviors, approves kernel/quantization changes for integrated flows.
- Solutions Eng / SE: provides partner integration templates and assists with SDK behavior tuning.
- Oncall (days of activation): stands up a temporary oncall rotation with the partner for first 72 hrs of production traffic.

Integration readiness checklist (must pass before >5% traffic):
1) Contract review: request patterns, retry/backoff semantics documented (owner: Integration Owner).
2) Baseline tests: synthetic traffic against staging with realistic concurrency (owner: SE + Integration Owner).
3) Observability: dashboards created, P95/P99, error-rate, KV cache hit rate, and request size histograms (owner: SRE).
4) Canary plan: incremental traffic ramp plan with explicit gating thresholds and rollback criteria (owner: SRE + Runtime Eng).
5) Rate-limit and quota configuration: ensure partner has sensible client-side limits to avoid thundering herd (owner: Integration Owner).
6) Failure injection: run at least one simulated failure (latency spike / outage) and verify graceful degradation paths (owner: SRE).
7) Compliance check (if private deployment): network egress rules and KMS integration validated (owner: Security & Private Deployments).
8) Playbook & escalation contacts documented in Slack and oncall rotation set up (owner: Integration Owner).

Communication & escalation pattern:
- Pre-launch: weekly sync 3 weeks out, then daily standups 3 days out for high-risk integrations.
- Activation day: EOD status notes in #sre-integrations, live bridge if any gate trips.
- Escalation ladder: partner PM -> Integration Owner -> SRE Liaison -> Runtime Eng -> Head of SRE.
- Bridge templates: use /bridges/start-integration with fields: partner, integration-owner, expected traffic, canary thresholds, rollback command.

Canary & rollout gating (example):
- Phase 0: internal-only staging tests, pass 100% of health checks for 24h.
- Phase 1: 1% of traffic for 1 hour; no SLO regressions and error-rate delta < 0.05%.
- Phase 2: 5% traffic for 4 hours; P95 latency delta < 15% and no model-quality alerts.
- Phase 3: 20% for 24 hours; final sign-off if observability signals stable.
- Auto-rollback triggers: error-rate spike > 0.5% absolute, P95 latency increase > 50% or model-quality drop > 3%.

Observability signals (recommended panels & alerts):
- SLO burn-rate (30d) per integration, with link to incident playbook.
- Top contributing endpoints and partner-client IPs.
- Batching queue depth, KV cache hit/miss, and backend GPU utilization.
- Model drift metric: comparison on canonical prompt set, per-model-pass/fail rate.

Risk taxonomy and mitigations:
- Thundering retries: enforce client-side backoff + per-customer concurrency caps.
- SDK changes causing long-tail GC: require SDK upgrade window and memory diagnostics.
- Vendor region outage: fallback routing policy to alternate region/model variant.
- Data contract mismatch (schema drift): conservative validation and version pinning.

30/60/90 day experiment plan (activation cadence for new cohort):
- 0–30 days: rapid discovery — identify 10 highest-risk integrations, run contract checks, enable dashboards.
- 31–60 days: small cohort pilots — roll out canaries with 2-3 partners, iterate checklist and automation.
- 61–90 days: scale playbook — graduate partners to self-serve templates, measure reductions in manual intervention.

Checklist for post-incident follow-up (if integration caused breach):
- Timeline reconstruction (who, what, when), link to logs and traces.
- Root cause with contributing factors (including partner actions).
- Action items: code fix, config change, partner process change.
- Update runbook and checklist, retract or expand gate criteria as needed.

Quick templates (copy/paste):
- Canary Slack ping: "canary-start partner=ACME integration=sync-api phase=1 1% for 1h gate=P95<1.15x baseline"
- Rollback command (ops): "POST /admin/integrations/rollback?integration=sync-api&reason=canary-failure"

Open questions / TODOs:
- How to automate SDK upgrade windows? (investigate partner CI hooks)
- Should we require partner-side chaos testing? threshold?
- Determine SLA language for partner contracts about retry/backoff.

Appendix: sample linked artifacts and notes
- Confluence: Integration testing templates — https://confluence.redwood/inference/sre/integration-testing-templates
- Sample Jira tickets: INTEG-4510 (ACME canary), INTEG-4522 (SDK GC investigation)
- GitHub runtime PR: https://github.com/redwood-inference/runtime/pull/987 - note: changed batching window default from 16ms to 8ms (impact analysis in comments).

Notes to self / informal thoughts (scratch area):
- Consider a small "partner lab" rotation where SE pairs with partner engineers for first 48h. Good trade-off for high-revenue integrations.
- Lean on Optimize team for recommendations on quantization impact when partner signals high throughput.
- Add a short form for integration owners to declare expected token distribution and sequence lengths (helps runtime kernel selection).

Next steps (owners assigned):
- Priya: finalize 30/60/90 experiment plan and present at SRE sync 2026-02-15.
- Ethan: prototype canary automation runbook (Jenkins/GHA) by 2026-02-28.
- Marta: build dashboard template and alert playbook (grafana + slack actions) by 2026-03-05.

End of draft.
